result.title: What Egocentric Video Embeddings Encode and How to Combine Them with Inertial Sensors for Human Activity Recognition
result.comment: 31 pages, 11 figures, 11 tables. Solution to the 3rd WEAR Dataset Challenge @ HASCA 2026
result.summary: Egocentric video and body-worn inertial sensors are increasingly recorded together, and the video is usually encoded by pretrained models. What these embeddings represent when the camera sits on the head, and how they should be combined with inertial sensing, has received little attention. Across VideoMAEv2, CLIP, DINOv2 and the egocentric VC-1, the leading principal directions of the embedding are dominated by where the camera looks. Measured head orientation explains them on Ego-Exo4D for egocentric (R^2 0.49-0.70) but not exocentric cameras, and the scene layout explains them on WEAR. The part that the limbs' inertial signals predict separates activities across people. In a set-level probe, the rest separates exercise sets within a participant but not activities across people. This is consistent with separate roles: the video finds the clips of the same set, and the inertial classifier labels them. On WEAR, with temporal order removed and one random limb per one-second clip, we propagate inertial predictions over a within-participant video graph whose leading components are removed. This raises subject-wise cross-validated macro-F1 from 0.648 to 0.852. In our comparisons, propagation helps only over the video graph, and fusing the modalities in one classifier, or adding inertial edges to the graph, performs worse.

AI.brief_summary: 论文考察 egocentric 视频嵌入究竟编码了什么——在 VideoMAEv2、CLIP、DINOv2、VC-1 中主成分被「相机看向何处」主导（可由头部朝向、场景布局解释），并据此设计视频嵌入与惯性传感器的结合：去除主导成分后在组内视频图上传播惯性预测，使被试级 macro-F1 从 0.648 升至 0.852。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用探针拆解嵌入主方向、区分任务相关与视角/布局等干扰成分，并让两种模态分工（视频圈出同集合片段、惯性给标签）的做法，可能为核查 LVR 中视觉状态是否保留任务必要信息、以及 latent 相似度受内容与位置/视角混淆影响提供线索。
